title: Forestiere Underground Gardens – Fresno, California
seoTitle: Charter Bus to Forestiere Underground Gardens, Fresno
excerpt: A charter bus to Forestiere Underground Gardens in Fresno suits garden clubs, school groups and senior trips. Tour rules, vehicle sizing and the best season.

extraImage.alt: A citrus tree growing beneath a skylight in an underground courtyard at Forestiere Underground Gardens

body.text: Baldasare Forestiere arrived in Fresno from Sicily and found the land he had bought was hardpan, and the summers were brutal. So he dug. Over roughly forty years, starting in 1906, he hand-excavated a network of tunnels, courtyards and planting rooms across about ten acres, with skylights arranged so that fruit trees could grow underground. It is one of the strangest and most affecting places in California, and a charter bus to Forestiere Underground Gardens makes it a straightforward stop for a group that would otherwise never find it.
Why it works so well for a group

Most group attractions ask everyone to walk a long way or stand in the sun. This one does neither. The tour is guided, it moves at a conversational pace, and it is genuinely cool underground — often ten to twenty degrees below the surface temperature, which in a Fresno July is the difference between an enjoyable hour and an endured one.

It also lands with a very wide range of groups. Garden clubs come for the horticulture, school groups for the engineering, historical societies for the immigrant story, and senior excursions because it is interesting, shaded and not physically demanding. Very few destinations satisfy all four.

items: Guided tours only. You cannot wander the site independently, which means group size and arrival time have to be arranged in advance rather than decided on the day.
Around an hour underground, on uneven hand-cut floors with steps and low headroom in places. Sensible shoes matter more than usual.
Skylit courtyards where citrus, grapes and other fruit still grow below ground level — the part that surprises people who arrived expecting a novelty tunnel.
Seasonal opening. Hours are reduced outside the main season and the site closes for parts of the winter, so confirm the calendar before you set a date.

body.text: Group bookings should be made directly with the gardens well ahead of the visit. Tour capacity is limited by the passages themselves, and a group of forty will normally be split across staggered start times rather than taken through as one party.
Which charter bus fits the visit
The site sits just off Highway 99 on the north side of Fresno with straightforward road access, so the vehicle choice is about your group rather than the destination.

items: Forty to fifty-six: a full-size [charter bus](/fleet/charter-buses) is the right call if the gardens are one stop on a longer Central Valley itinerary, with luggage bays and an on-board restroom for the drive.
Twenty to thirty-two: a [mini bus](/fleet/mini-buses) matches the tour group sizes the site handles most easily and parks with less fuss.
Ten to fourteen: a [sprinter van](/fleet/sprinter-vans) suits a garden club or a small historical society outing.

body.text: School groups are a large share of the visitors here, and our [school trip transportation](/services/school-trips) quotes include the insurance documentation districts ask for as standard rather than on request.
Getting there, and what else to build around it

The gardens are a ninety-minute visit, not a day, which makes them a component rather than a destination. The sensible move is to pair them with something else in the region. Fresno sits within two and a half hours of Yosemite Valley and about an hour and a half from Sequoia and Kings Canyon, and the Forestiere site works well as a morning stop on the way to either.

We run pickups from [Fresno](/locations/california/fresno), [Visalia](/locations/california/visalia) and [Bakersfield](/locations/california/bakersfield), and from further afield for groups building a Central Valley itinerary. If you are searching for charter bus rental near me for a club or society outing, ask for the vehicle to stay with the group for the day rather than booking a drop-off and a return — the cost difference is usually small and it turns a single stop into a flexible day.

items: April to June: warm above ground, comfortable below, and the plantings are at their best.

July and August: Fresno regularly exceeds 100 degrees, which is precisely what the gardens were built to escape. The contrast is the point, but plan an early slot and keep the group out of the afternoon sun.
September and October: mild and quiet, and the easiest time to secure a group tour slot at short notice.
Winter: reduced hours and periodic closures. Always confirm before booking a vehicle.

body.text: One practical warning about photography. The passages are dim and the courtyards are bright, which is a difficult combination for phone cameras and a frustrating one for a group that came to take pictures. Anyone serious about photographing the site should plan for a mid-morning slot, when the skylights are doing the most work, rather than a late-afternoon one.
